about: What core-hook-npm-response.py expects of the pre hook's first three npm asks (prefix, root, config), and of its own readers and lifecycle. It was written by reading the product source statically at the line ranges each cite names, and the ask contract in AGENTS.md, and declaring a synthetic fixture's expected results from that reading. No product ask was run to produce it, and no run's output or candidate record was read to produce it. A role is named by the request the expectation declares (argv template and working directory) and by the source's call slot. It is never named from a claim number, a completion order or a value the hook produced. Every fact the collector keeps is observed with its value, absent with its basis, or unavailable with the operation that did not answer; a comparison is a match, a mismatch of two observed values, or incomparable. Placeholders: @W@ the statement's words, @Q@ the quiet flags, @S@ one ask group's scratch directory, @BOX@ @PROJECT@ @HOME@ @STATE@ @TMP@ the sandbox, @SYSTEM@ the system directories on the hook's PATH. A relation candidate covers one group, the initial attempt and its three roles; another group, a follow-up attempt and a declared shared effect are reported apart.

ps.cite: macOS ps(1): '-p Display information about processes which match the specified process IDs.' The manual has no EXIT STATUS section.
ps.query: one ps call is one record: purpose, argv, fields, the collector's own pid (the sentinel), the targets, locale C, the timeout, start and end times, and the outcome (exit with its status, signal, timeout or exception) with stdout and stderr as they came
ps.read: read_ps reads a record only when every field is there with its type, the argv is the one its purpose's fields, its targets and the sentinel make, ps exited by itself with a status, stderr is empty, every line reads as the fields, the sentinel's row is there and no row names a pid nobody asked about; otherwise the answer is unavailable and is no exit, no completion and no reason to let a next child go
ps.exit: with a row for the pid and the start time read when the child started: Z is a zombie, another start time is another process (pid-reused), the same start time is alive; without that start time the row is not attributed
ps.absence: a missing row means no process only under a ps host fact record selected by digest whose expectation held, and only for a query whose status is the one that record measured for an answer with a missing pid; without one a missing row is unavailable

host_fact.measure: the collector starts a child that ends when its input closes, asks ps for it alive, closes its input and reaps it, starts a second such child, then asks for the first alone and for both; nothing is signalled
host_fact.expect: alive: rows include the sentinel and the first child, not a zombie; gone: rows are exactly the sentinel; mixed: rows are exactly the sentinel and the second child; the gone and mixed queries exited with the same status, which becomes the absence status; the first child was reaped before the gone query started

scenarios.name: P0-natural
scenarios.about: Every child answers and is let go as soon as its output was read; the claim and completion orders are whatever happened, and are recorded.

scenarios.name: P1-permuted
scenarios.about: The observer lets the children claim their record numbers in one order and exit in another, each different from the source's start order.

scenarios.name: P2-permuted
scenarios.about: A second claim order and a second completion order, each different from P1's and from the start order.

scenarios.name: N3a-slot-swap
scenarios.about: Every request, record and child output is the positive's. After all three children wrote and before any was let go, the observer exchanges the prefix and root response files in the hook's scratch directory, so the hook reads each of the two roles from the other's file.

scenarios.name: N3b-output-swap
scenarios.about: Every request is the positive's and every record names the positive's answer, but the root child writes the config answer's bytes to its own stdout and stderr and the config child writes the root answer's. Each child keeps its own exit status.

npm_fetch.unknown: npm was not asked which registry this install fetches from: no npm install in this command named where it lands

scenarios.name: N4-follow
scenarios.about: The initial config ask is refused with ENOWORKSPACES, so the hook asks config again in a new group, in the directory the prefix answer named. The follow-up depends on the prefix answer and is outside the initial relation; the hook's fetch facts come from it.

declared.about: Inputs made from a live launch's own records by named edits, judged by the same oracle and read_pending. D0-D9 test what the oracle does with a missing, duplicated, misplaced or unobserved child and a declared shared effect; J3v put writer-shaped and damaged npm_fetch values into a real exchange's pending record. They are synthetic and are no evidence about a real npm, a real ENOWORKSPACES or a real cache.

edits.effect: the root child reads a file the prefix child writes

value.unknown: npm config failed (exit 1: x), so safedeps cannot tell which registry this install fetches from

controls.about: The author's own controls of this change's boundaries, each with literal inputs and literal expectations. readers and adapters run in the check subcommand; copies and sensitivity run from copies of the tree with the exact edits named, and check-controls reads what they left with the standard library and the status their parent saw. A sensitivity control removes one boundary from a copy and must make the named cases or checks fail. None of these is evidence about a real ps failure, a real slot race or a real npm, and none is an independent verification.

The observer must take no exit from it, give the order up within its budget and let no next child go before it gave up.

copies.about: After the observer started and wrote records, its first release raises, and so does its cleanup's. The collector must end the observer's launch as stopped (exit 2) once the observer ended, keep the journal with its terminal exception and cleanup error, start no next launch and publish no manifest. No hook child is released by the observer; each goes on after its own hold.

not_observed: an exit status's value from outside the hook: macOS gives a process's exit status to its parent, and the observer is not the parent of an ask child; the value is the child's own record and the hook's consumption of it
which bytes the hook read: the observer reads the response files while the child is held and the hook's result depends on them, but no read by the hook is traced
the launch order of the three children: the source starts them in one order (the slots above); nothing here observes the start itself
a process's absence without a ps host fact: a missing row is unavailable unless a selected host fact record measured what an answer with a missing pid looks like

time: whether the order budget, the children's starts, the ps calls, file I/O and a follow-up config fit inside the hook's shared ask deadline is not measured; an order the observer could not impose within its budget is reported not observed
an observer that never ends: the collector waits for it without a signal, so its final status is not reached and the run's pending record is what remains
real npm: every answer comes from the stand-in; a real npm's shared cache, configuration files and ENOWORKSPACES are not exercised
